newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end firmer on late momentum.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end firmer on late momentum.

text.p: Singapore shares picked up some momentum late Thursday to end higher after a session dominated by selected demand for blue chips and over-the-counter issues.
Dealers said volume improved in the afternoon, triggered by speculation in some counters and when European markets opened.
"Some banks recovered their losses with volume picking up overall, including on the losers," a dealer with a local bank said, noting cautious buying from foreign funds.
The UOB OTC index of Malaysian stocks rose 12.98 points to 1,158.83. The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 7.72 points at 2,061.71 on an active turnover of 210 million.
The spillover firm mood from the Kuala Lumpur bourse also underpined the Singapore market, already encouraged by a rise of 5.9 percent in April export figures on Tuesday, dealers said.
Gainers included Parkway Holdings, which rose to a new high of Singapore $6.70 and closed up 20 cents at $6.65. Dealers said rumours of Temasek buying equity in Parkway encouraged buying.
Delifrance also hit a new high of S$1.83, closing up eight cents at S$1.80, on rumours of a new franchise in Indonesia.
Topping volume was HongKong Land, down four cents at S$2.65, paring earlier gains. DBS, OCBC and UOB foreign tranches came off lows but ended weaker.--Jacqueline Wong (65 8703080)
